clauses.reason: Terminated by statutory repeal on 1935-06-14. The report command (paragraph 6) directs the Code Authority to submit to the Administrator a study of hours, rates of pay and conditions three months after the code's effective date, as a condition of the approval. The three-month period is a report deadline and is not an end; the command depends on the code and the Code Authority the code creates. The order states no period, condition or date of its own, so it has no own-terms end. Its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I: under 3(b) the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, a violation in or affecting interstate commerce was an unfair method of competition, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 (49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, approved June 14, 1935) provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed' and states no later effective date, so the approval's prospective operative effect ended when the resolution was approved. Actor: the Congress by Senate Joint Resolution 113. The date is the resolution's approval date, not a general rule's default: the repeal reaches this command because the command had legal effect only through the repealed provisions. June 16, 1935 is not an end (section 1 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936). Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization recorded in source_notes, not an end date.

inventory_overrides.reason: Item 6 is the only command among the six enumerated paragraphs: it directs the Code Authority to submit a study to the Administrator. Items 1 to 5 are the President's findings under section 3(a) (application made, notice and hearings given, code complies, code will effectuate the policy) and command nothing; the machine inventory listed them as clauses and omitted the approval.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: EO 6686 is read in full in the registered American Presidency Project (APP) transcription jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6686-approval-code-fair-competition-for-the-linseed-oil-manufacturing.txt (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-29: the row with the same sha256 (2c1d3c3b47e4...) in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl is a common-crawl capture (, captured 2023-09-07T18:14:56Z, WARC location recorded so the page can be re-fetched) whose heading is 'Executive Order 6686—Approval of Code of Fair Competition for the Linseed Oil Manufacturing Industry' and whose date is 1934-04-20; that date agrees with the date line of the held text ('April 20, 1934.'), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held file is the whole order (recital, operative paragraph, signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line); it carries no order number, so the number comes from the page record. Clauses and sources are quoted from this registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record, the census register ('Executive Order 6686—Approval of Code of Fair Competition for the Linseed Oil Manufacturing Industry', 1934-04-20) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (printed page 576: 'Code of Fair Competition for the Linseed Oil Manufac turing Industry approved.'). The recital names the report of the Secretary of Agriculture and of the Administrator under EO 6182 as supplemented; the register and WPA titles both name the approval of the Linseed Oil code. EO 6686 (April 20, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) recites that the Secretary of Agriculture and the Administrator reported separately on the provisions within their respective jurisdictions, finds in five numbered paragraphs that the application, notice, hearings and statutory conditions were met, adds in paragraph 6 that 'Three months after the effective date of this Code, the Code Authority shall submit to the Administrator a study of the hours of labor, rates of pay, and other conditions of employment within this Industry', and in a final paragraph approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Linseed Oil Manufacturing Industry. The machine inventory was wrong (six clauses made of the findings; the approval omitted), so the inventory is corrected with two spans: the report command and the approval. Legal reading: both clauses depend on section 3. The approval has no period of its own. The report command is a condition of approval that section 3(a) expressly authorizes ('requirements for the making of reports'), addressed to the Code Authority the code creates; its three-month period is a deadline for a report, which under the owner's 2026-10-21 report-deadline ruling is not an end, and the code's effective date is not held, so the deadline could not be dated in any case. Both clauses end with the repeal on 1935-06-14.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No own-terms end for the approval. The report command's 'three months after the effective date of this Code' is a report deadline; it is not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21, report deadlines), no held record shows whether or when the study was submitted, and the code's effective date is not held. The command therefore stays on the books until its legal basis is removed on 1935-06-14. The name search found EO 6551 (January 1934), which transfers the Secretary of Agriculture's delegated functions to the Administrator and lists Linseed Oil among the first-processor industries for which certain exercises of those functions need the Secretary's written approval; it is a delegation order that predates this approval and does not cancel or suspend the code. No later held order names the Linseed Oil code. Searches made on 2026-10-29: (1) a full-text search of every held order text numbered 6200 through 7100 under jobs/*/output/texts (APP, HathiTrust GPO, Wikisource and Federal Register texts; clause-drafts copies excluded) for the code's name; (2) a citation search of the same texts for this order's number; (3) a search of the same texts for general NRA orders that could suspend, cancel or supersede codes: the held general orders (EO 6354 as amended by EO 6710, EO 6646, 6711, 6750-C, 6764 and 6829) prescribe rules, contract terms and delegations, and none suspends, cancels or supersedes the code named here; (4) the census register titles (jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv) and the WPA 1944 numbered list, read for this code's name; they show no cancellation, suspension or superseding code. Orders for which no text is held (for example EO 6454) could not be searched, so the search covers held texts only. No held record shows this code cancelled or modified under section 10(b), superseded by another code, revoked or suspended before June 14, 1935. June 16, 1935 is not an end: it was Title I's original two-year expiry under section 2(c), which section 1 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 replaced with April 1, 1936. The approved code's own text is not held (it is printed in the NRA Codes volumes the WPA list cites), so a code-internal expiry or effective-date term could not be read; no held order records one for this code. Schechter (295 U.S. 495, May 27, 1935) is recorded in source_notes as a validity characterization, not as an end date: it reversed one conviction and held the Live Poultry Code provisions invalid, it did not cancel or withdraw this approving order, and no held record shows this code cancelled or suspended on that date.","independent_command_check":"The report command is addressed to the Code Authority and concerns the hours, rates of pay and conditions 'within this Industry' as set forth in this code, with a view to revising them; it is a condition of the approval, not a delegation under another statute and not an appointment. It has its own end (the repeal) and its own deadline note. The order appoints no one and creates no body.","savings_check":"Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. Whether the Code Authority submitted the study is not shown in any held source; a study submitted before the repeal would be an accrued, completed act, and nothing in the order obliges anyone to submit one after the repeal.","scope_check":"Corrected inventory: (a) paragraph 6, the report command; (b) the final approval paragraph. savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. Whether the Code Authority submitted the study is not shown in any held source; a study submitted before the repeal would be an accrued, completed act, and nothing in the order obliges anyone to submit one after the repeal.
